fixture_limits: No authenticated socket, aggregate LoadFromDB execution, full Player::Update loop or7.3.5 client check is claimed. The fixture executes actual logout and the specified native prepared-load components in source order, using disposable character/auth schemas and read-only private World/Hotfix pools. It does not use personal account/character rows.

The controlled logout cases preserve the actual in-progress Infusion until logout; they do not manually interrupt casting or strip Corrupted before save. Pending-absorb cases use an ordinary ranged raid member and explicitly CombatStop that subject to isolate live-aura persistence from disconnect-death/repop. The native absorb, duration, caster and save filter remain intact. These cases are not an assertion that a melee-attacked disconnect will preserve a living Player.

Helya/other actor scheduling is frozen during the isolated subject observation. The full native phase bootstrap and later evade are real. Other fixture actors use health buffers. The subject is a Warrior fixture without a fully initialized client appearance/class resource/weapon/talent layout.

Input handoff, cast bar, aura icons, transform rendering, action bars, pet portrait, camera, sound, full raid/quest completion and a cold server restart remain client/integration checks. Reload after an active pending Axion reaches its native expiry in a continuing live encounter is not exercised here.
retained_failures: The initial reference used a second stack Map with an existing outdoor identity and logged a collision-tile double-unload diagnostic during fixture teardown. The corrected fixture reuses the managed outdoor zone; the final run does not emit that diagnostic. No collision-core change was made.

Two diagnostic Frostbolt interruption probes were inconclusive: one observed0 extra bursts with a default class cast-speed setup; after initializing the speed/time fields the next probe did not begin Frostbolt. Their failed logs are retained. No claim of an additional damaging proc exploit or reproduction of arbitrary class-spell interruption follows from them. The established production defect is the independently observed permanent orphan aura save/load. These diagnostics are absent from final acceptance tests.

An early current probe incorrectly expected pending Axion to be saveable. It failed its fixture assertion after mode0 had passed. That exception left an unowned heap Player/bind during static teardown and an access violation was observed in InstanceSaveManager destructor -> Player::UnbindInstance -> InstanceSave::RemovePlayer -> safe-mutex hash lookup. A later overly strict no-attacker setup assertion reached the same teardown failure. Final fixture ownership uses a unique_ptr until native logout takes ownership. These retained failures are not labeled a repaired production mutex defect.
